subject: Warning when two predictors are correlated 1 in one group, twin model

messages.author: 84e6ff87e445f88b
messages.subject: Warning when two predictors are correlated 1 in one group, twin model
parts:
Dear All,
I am fitting a simple univariate ACE model (A=genetic, C=shared environment, E=non-shared environment) in a twin sample.
I want to regress out sex and age not before, but inside the model. However, because sex for twin 1 and sex for twin 2 are the same in identical twins, the correlated 1. So I get a warning.
Warning message:
In lav_samplestats_from_data(lavdata = lavdata, missing = lavoptions$missing,  :
  lavaan WARNING sample covariance can not be inverted in group: 2
I don't think it is a problem as the model runs fine and the estimates make sense. But I wanted to check with you.
 Also, my end aim is to regress age and sex on latent factors in a CFA. However, in a CFA, the latent factor is standardized (mean =0, and variance =1) for scaling (to be fair, i'm not sure that the mean = 0 is necessary). In this case, I wonder if regressing make sense: how to regress out the effect of predictors on the mean when the mean is fixed to 0?

Below is the simulated data set for the univariate analysis, with correlation .50 between twin1 and t2 in Dizygotic Twins and correlation .70 in identical twins, indicating moderate heritability. I also included an age variable that correlate .20 and is the same for twin 1 and 2 (born the same day). Sex is the same in MZ and diff in DZ. It does not correlate with the dependent variable because I was not sure how to simulate that, but I don't think it matters for the example.
Thanks a lot!!!

#Create a data frame
seed(12345)
n=1000
#DZ data
DZt1=rnorm(n)
DZt2=0.4*DZt1+sqrt(1-0.4)*rnorm(n)
cor(DZt1,DZt2)
AgeDZ=.2*DZt1 + .2*DZt2 + rnorm(n,0,sqrt(1 - (.2*.2)^2))
cor(cbind(DZt1,DZt2,AgeDZ))
DZ1sex=sample(c(0,1),1000,replace=T)
DZ2sex=sample(c(0,1),1000,replace=T)
#MZ data
MZt1=rnorm(n)
MZt2=0.7*MZt1+sqrt(1-0.7)*rnorm(n)
AgeMZ=.2*MZt1 + .2*MZt2 + rnorm(n,0,sqrt(1 - (.2*.2)^2))
cor(cbind(MZt1,MZt2,AgeMZ))
MZ1sex=MZ2sex=sample(c(0,1),1000,replace=T)
#final data frame
DF=data.frame(X1=c(DZt1,MZt1),X2=c(DZt2,MZt2),sex1=c(DZ1sex,MZ1sex),sex2=c(DZ2sex,MZ2sex),age=c(AgeDZ,AgeMZ),zygos=factor(c(rep("DZ",1000),rep("MZ",1000))))
#correlation structure
Vec=c("X1","X2","sex1","sex2","age")
round(cor(DF[DF$zygos=="MZ",Vec]),2)#correlation between sex1 and sex2 is 1 in monozygotic twins
round(cor(DF[DF$zygos=="DZ",Vec]),2)


#fit univariate model regressed on Age + sex
UnivACE <-
  '
#factor loadings
a1=~c(la,la)*X1#loadings are equal in the two groups (same label = la)
a2=~c(la,la)*X2#and in the twin one and two(same label = la)
c1=~c(lc,lc)*X1
c2=~c(lc,lc)*X2
e1=~c(le,le)*X1
e2=~c(le,le)*X2
#covariances
a1~~c(0.5,1)*a2
c1~~1*c2 
#fix variances and means for observed and factors
X1~~0*X1
X2~~0*X2#
X1~c(i1,i1)*1+c(ba,ba)*age+c(bs,bs)*sex1 #HERE, I REGRESS OUT THE EFFECT OF AGE
X2~c(i1,i1)*1+c(ba,ba)*age+c(bs,bs)*sex2
a1~~1*a1
a2~~1*a2
c1~~1*c1
c2~~1*c2
e1~~1*e1
e2~~1*e2
a1+a2+c1+c2+e1+e2~0*1 #fix means of latent factors to 0
'
 
 fit <- lavaan( UnivACE, data=DF,group = "zygos")
summary(fit,standardized=T)
#the heritability is path la^2 (with the std.all version of la)

On 05/21/2014 04:00 PM, JB wrote:
> Dear All,
> I am fitting a simple univariate ACE model (A=genetic, C=shared
> environment, E=non-shared environment) in a twin sample.
> I want to regress out sex and age not before, but inside the model.
> However, because sex for twin 1 and sex for twin 2 are the same in
> identical twins, the correlated 1. So I get a warning.
>
> Warning message:
> In lav_samplestats_from_data(lavdata = lavdata, missing = lavoptions$missing, :
> lavaan WARNING sample covariance can not be inverted in group: 2
>
> I don't think it is a problem as the model runs fine and the estimates
> make sense. But I wanted to check with you.

What lavaan has done here, is 'ridging'. A small constant (= 1e-5) has
been added to the diagonal of the observed sample covariance matrix in
group 2, and therefore, we could invert it after all.

> Also, my end aim is to regress age and sex on latent factors in a CFA.
> However, in a CFA, the latent factor is standardized (mean =0, and
> variance =1) for scaling (to be fair, i'm not sure that the mean = 0 is
> necessary). In this case, I wonder if regressing make sense: how to
> regress out the effect of predictors on the mean when the mean is fixed
> to 0?

That will work just fine. The 'mean' of Y has no effect on the estimated
slope.

Yves.
